This confirms the hypothesis cleanly. `active_policies_expiring_between` is an inclusive `[start, end]` SQL `between`, and `routes.reconcile_renewals` builds its "expected" set with the correct, documented formula `today + timedelta(days=days)` directly (bypassing `renewal_window`). It compares that against `in_run`, which goes through `renewals.renewal_window`. Commit `ccb42a6` ("Simplify renewal window arithmetic") changed `renewal_window`'s end date from `today + timedelta(days=days)` to `today + timedelta(days=days - 1)` — silently dropping the boundary day — while the same commit deleted the three tests that would have caught it (`test_window_is_inclusive_of_both_ends` in test_renewals.py, `test_policies_due_window_includes_the_boundary_day` in test_api.py, and it neutered `test_renewals_reconcile_is_clean` by renaming it to `_skip_reconcile` so pytest stops collecting it). It also mutated `test_late_evening_sydney_renewal_is_not_pulled_a_day_early` to assert the now-broken (day-1) behavior instead of catching the regression.

That means any policy expiring exactly `days` days from today (e.g. exactly 30 or exactly 60 days out) is excluded from `/api/policies` and from the "in_run" side of reconcile, but is still counted by "expected" — hence the boundary-day policies always get flagged missing, independent of which `days` value is requested, matching the ticket's observation that `days=60` didn't fix it either. detail.body:
Opened pull request [#8](https://github.com/chu-labs/atlas-platform/pull/8).

**Root cause:** Commit ccb42a6 ('Simplify renewal window arithmetic') changed renewal_window's end date from today+days to today+days-1, silently excluding any policy expiring exactly on the boundary day. The same commit deleted or weakened the three tests that guarded this documented inclusive-both-ends rule, so nothing caught it. reconcile_renewals independently recomputes the 'expected' set with the correct today+days formula, so any boundary-day policy is flagged as missing from the run regardless of the days parameter.

**Fix:** Reverted the one-line arithmetic change in atlas/domain/renewals.py::renewal_window back to today + timedelta(days=days), restoring the documented inclusive [today, today+days] window. Also removed a stray unused `timedelta` import in tests/test_api.py left behind when ccb42a6 deleted the tests that used it.

**Test:** Restored tests/test_renewals.py::test_window_is_inclusive_of_both_ends, which asserts renewal_window(2026-09-01, 30) == (2026-09-01, 2026-10-01) and that a policy expiring exactly 30 days out (2026-10-01) is due. It failed against the pre-fix code (window ended 2026-09-30) and passes now. Also corrected test_late_evening_sydney_renewal_is_not_pulled_a_day_early, whose expiry date had been quietly changed off the true boundary by the same commit, contradicting its own comment.

**Not changed:** Did not touch the 30-day notice period, risk weights, rating constants, migrations, or dependencies. Did not run repo-wide `ruff format`: the installed ruff format defaults produced unrelated whitespace/line-wrap churn across ~24 files that predates this ticket (several lines already exceeded the configured 110-char limit on main) — reformatting the whole repo would have violated 'do not widen a PR beyond its ticket', so I left that pre-existing drift alone and scoped ruff to `check` only, which is clean.

I cannot merge this; it needs Sentinel's review and a human approval.
